verdict: Use it for how far a stock could move, not which way.

items.title: Price ranges (the cone)
items.finding: The shaded cone is honest about how far prices move. On 2019 to today, a period none of the tuning saw, about 8 in 10 real outcomes landed inside the 80% cone, slightly fewer at 1 and 3 months because of the 2020 crash and 2022 bear market. The old cone was clearly worse.
items.numbers: Inside the 80% cone, 2019+: 80% at 1 week, 78.5% at 1 month, 78% at 3 months (old cone: 79%, 76%, 76%). 159 stocks, about 52,000 forecasts per horizon.

items.title: Will this stock go up or down?
items.finding: No model beat simply guessing each stock’s usual direction, on any horizon. The “Chance it ends higher” figure is a lean, not a call.
items.numbers: 2019+: the cone's middle line called the direction right 53% / 55% / 58% of the time (1W / 1M / 3M) vs 54% / 56% / 58% for guessing each stock's usual direction.

items.title: Which stocks beat the others (momentum)
items.finding: Stocks that rose most over the past year tended to beat the rest, a little. The honest edge is about 2-3% a year among established large caps, not statistically reliable, and nothing on volatile small caps.
items.numbers: The big 2019+ numbers were mostly hindsight in the stock list: today’s list is full of stocks that are in it because they already won.

items.title: Market timing (200-day average)
items.finding: Stepping out of the market when the S&P 500 drops below its 200-day average cut the worst crashes before 2019, but it gave up too much return since.
items.numbers: 2019+: about 8% a year, vs 16% for just holding.

items.title: Earnings weeks
items.finding: Weeks likely to contain earnings are riskier. From price and volume alone they can only be spotted roughly, so widening the cone for them gained too little to use.
items.numbers: A week flagged as likely held a real earnings-sized move only about 1 time in 7.

use_for: Knowing when a stock is unusually jumpy
